cases.name: Deborah Will
cases.narrative: On 6/22/1993, her body was discovered by her then-boyfriend, Kenneth Logan, in the back seat of her Chevrolet Blazer, which was parked near railroad tracks a few blocks away from Erisco Industries, a wire-forming factory in Erie, PA at which both Will and Hardy worked. Will had been strangled with twine, and her clothes were notably dirty. Due to the type of twine and the chemical composition of the dirt, investigators came to believe that Will had been killed at the Erisco plant. This assumption was bolstered by the discovery of a threaded bolt under Will’s body, which was consistent with a missing bolt that was used to lock the gate to a loading dock at Erisco. There were signs of a struggle. Flesh was found under Will’s fingernails, blood stained the back of her shirt, and ligature marks appeared on and around her neck. Seminal fluid was detected in her vagina and on her underwear. Investigators also discovered a used condom near Will’s vehicle, along with a card from an establishment called the Jockey Health Club.

cases.name: Selena Shara' Wall
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Selena attended East High School. She worked at the Salvation Army and later joined her family business as a bartender. Selena enjoyed traveling, summer vacations, and being with her family and friends. But most of all, she loved her son." Her mom Debra Wall said her daughter was a warm, caring person who was very positive. She cared about her son and did a lot of things with her nieces, nephews and the children of her friends, she said. "She was a good friend to all her friends. I felt she was my best friend," Wall said.

cases.name: Lora Lee Roberts
cases.about:
Her obituary said: "Lora graduated from Strong Vincent High School. Lora was a devoted mother, loving fiancé, who cherished her family members, and dear friends whose heart touched countless lives.

Lora dedicated her life to helping others, passionately advocating for the homeless, survivors of domestic abuse and anyone in need. She worked as a nurse’s aide for nearly a decade, spending much of her career at Presbyterian Homes and Manchester Commons. A natural caregiver, she loved her work and was pursuing her nursing degree. She also served as a former board member of Community of Caring and was honored as one of Mercy Center’s Alumni of the year. Above all, Lora loved her family.

Lora will be remembered for her enormous heart, unwavering compassion, and willingness to stand up for those who needed a voice. She was a hero to many, and the lives she touched will never be the same because of her love and kindness. Though her life was far too short her legacy will live on through her children, her community, and everyone fortunate enough to have known her. She will be deeply missed, forever loved, and never forgotten."
